blockingFindings.summary: Active higher-isolation transaction with an old snapshot can drop a table containing a newly committed goal.
blockingFindings.mechanism: ACCESS EXCLUSIVE prevents concurrent writes but does not refresh an existing REPEATABLE READ or SERIALIZABLE transaction snapshot. The emptiness query then misses a committed goal and DROP executes. The migration currently checks only transaction activity, not snapshot/isolation safety.
reproduction: Start reverting QueryRunner in REPEATABLE READ or SERIALIZABLE.
SELECT count(*) FROM migrations establishes its snapshot without reading/locking learning_goals.
A separate DataSource connection inserts and commits a synthetic learning goal. An outside count sees one row.
Invoke the actual compiled migration down(reverting). It returns successfully and to_regclass(learning_goals) is NULL inside that transaction.
Always ROLLBACK the destructive transaction, verify the committed goal is restored/preserved, then drop only the generated review database.
blockingFindings.control: The same interleaving under READ COMMITTED correctly rejects with Cannot roll back learning goals with saved goals.
blockingFindings.recommendedCorrection: Fail closed on unsupported transaction isolation before destructive work, or otherwise establish/prove a fresh snapshot. Explicitly requiring READ COMMITTED is a narrow correction; add regression cases for old-snapshot REPEATABLE READ and SERIALIZABLE.
blockingFindings.sourceExplanation: PostgreSQL documents that LOCK after an earlier SELECT does not refresh REPEATABLE READ/SERIALIZABLE visibility.

actualResults.error: Cannot roll back learning goals with saved goals; preserve goal history before reverting.

reproduction.cleanup: All destructive transaction effects rolled back; generated database dropped; owned PostgreSQL and Redis processes stopped.
